stop_condition: Every item in the operator's WHAT TO VERIFY list is traced to a result: the curl/branch/checkout refusal forms and both re-check hints verified BY EXECUTION with the host bd hashed around every probe; install.ps1 judged by reading plus an independent (non-test) render of its procedure against install.sh's executed output; the seven L1 specs, L2 installer specs and lint re-run to rc; every proposition sweep run with a positive control; the manifest regenerated from git archive; and no finding at or above high remains in the installer's printed procedure or the release text.

findings.evidence: PROSE. Falsified proposition: the mechanism (installer-flags.test.sh driving install.sh's unpinned upgrade over the host's bd) was found IN CI by hashing bd before and after every spec. The new comment reads '(found in CI by hashing bd before and after every spec)'. THE RECORD SAYS A CONTAINER, TWICE: (1) 71e1d16's own commit message, `git log -1 --format=%B 71e1d16 | sed -n 3,4p` -> 'THE ROOT CAUSE of META-TEST 8a's failure, found by hashing /usr/local/bin/bd before and after every L1 spec in a container'; (2) .github/workflows/test.yml:233-234, SHIPPED and NOT touched by this diff, `sed -n 233,234p .github/workflows/test.yml` -> 'THE AGENT, named by hashing /usr/local/bin/bd before and after every spec in a container: installer-flags.test.sh.' The README's parallel sentence (unchanged here, README.md:402-403) claims no location at all: 'The cause, found by hashing bd before and after every spec'. And no CI-side hashing could have found it: the BD-CANARY is the per-spec bd hash and it was ADDED BY the fix commit 71e1d16 (`grep -n BD-CANARY-ARM .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh` -> 2031), with wyt3's own CI record for run 37187557586 on 71e1d16 reporting it 'ARMED ... No runner-level trip'. So the one surface that names a location now names the wrong one, and contradicts another file in the same change set's own repository.
findings.description: A measurement-provenance error in the doctor's own header, in a release whose thesis is that no claim ships that nothing checks, and in the same comment block this commit otherwise TIGHTENED (it correctly weakened 'Its lane did NOT measure it until 2026-10-02' to 'its lane's green history is consistent with never having measured it'). Behaviour is unaffected and nothing a reader would DO changes, which is why this is medium and not high. UNVERIFIED SUGGESTION -- verify before adoption: replace 'found in CI by hashing bd before and after every spec' with 'found by hashing bd before and after every spec in a container'. One word, and it then matches test.yml, the commit message and the README.

findings.evidence: PROSE. Proposition stated flat, in the voice of an observation: the DEVELOPMENT HOST's bd 1.1.2 -> 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2 was replaced by the installer's upgrade step ('bd did not upgrade itself; this repo's own installer replaced it'; printed text: 'its own installer ... replaced its bd 1.1.2 -> 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2 across one work arc'). The record hedges for exactly this population: 71e1d16's commit message says 'On developer hosts it is the most plausible cause of unexplained bd upgrades.' The hashing experiment observed the mechanism firing IN A CONTAINER running the same spec; no before/after hash was ever taken on the dev host for those three moves. I CANNOT SHOW THE CLAIM FALSE AND THE SUPPORT IS STRONG: the mechanism provably existed continuously (`git log -S BD_UPGRADE_COMMAND -- install.sh` -> fdfd6ce 2026-08-03 introduced the unpinned default, 71e1d16 removed it); the 0.99.0 fixture that triggers it predates that (`git log -G '0\.99\.0' -- .claude/scripts/tests/installer-flags.test.sh` -> 7c3a175 2026-07-27, and nothing else touched it in between); the floor was already 1.1.2 at fdfd6ce (`git show fdfd6ce:install.sh | grep RECOMMENDED_BD_VERSION=` -> 1.1.2), so 0.99.0 was below it on every run; the observed versions track 'newest release at the time' (omwx records the host on 1.2.1 by 2026-08-13, 1.2.2 released 2026-08-15, 1.3.0 released 2026-09-15), which is the signature of an unpinned install-latest; and the bd-self-upgrade alternative was TESTED and did not reproduce (wyt3 comment 2026-10-01T20:04:16Z: after bd init/doctor/list in a bd-1.1.2 container with network, 'the binary's version, size and mtime are UNCHANGED').
findings.description: Inference in the voice of an observation, scoped to the dev-host application only; the MECHANISM itself was observed. Filed for the record rather than as an objection: it is a strict improvement on the unhedged 'bd self-upgraded' it replaces (which the same wyt3 comment falsified), and the operator's direction named the installer step as 'the established cause'. Severity calibrated against this project's own precedent for the identical class: docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-ishe-r3.json R3-F4 filed 'inference in the voice of an observation' at MEDIUM and explicitly not a v5.0.0 blocker; this one is weaker still, so low. UNVERIFIED SUGGESTION -- verify before adoption: keep the mechanism and mark only its dev-host application, e.g. '... bd did not upgrade itself; the same installer step was observed replacing a host's bd in a container, and it is what replaced this one.'

findings.evidence: PROSE, residual of the framing operator item (6) asked to be replaced. The line reads 'That is not softened here because opt-in users should see the cost profile before choosing.' It sits inside the same [5.0.0] block whose headline this commit rewrote to 'THE DESIGN PHASE IS OPT-OUT PER TASK' and whose other three opt-in sites were converted (CHANGELOG:21, :40, :164; README:204, :213; RELEASE_AUDIT:807). Sweep method: git ls-files, leading comment/blockquote markers stripped, whitespace collapsed, 2-line window so a wrapped phrase is still caught; the only other live 'opt-in' hits are CHANGELOG:329 (a mode=rollup function parameter) and CHANGELOG:4118-4120 (v3-era /effort), both different propositions, and README:249 ('the cost you are actually opting into'), which is correct under either framing.
findings.description: Not false -- a task that takes the design phase does opt into it, per task -- but it names a USER CLASS ('opt-in users') that the new framing says does not exist: every task either takes the phase or declines it. Terminological inconsistency inside the paragraph that carries the release's headline decision. UNVERIFIED SUGGESTION -- verify before adoption: '... because anyone choosing to take the design phase should see the cost profile first.'

findings.location: install.sh:2478 and install.sh:2591-2593 (disclosure (b), filed as claude-workflow-plugin-hevd)
findings.evidence: NON-BLOCKING, and a correction to a DISCLOSURE rather than to shipped text. Disclosure (b) says of the deferred same-class sites: 'None of them is on the procedure's path.' Two of them are reachable from the procedure's own step 3, in a failure sub-case. mcp_deps_manual_hint (install.sh:2469-2479) prints 'bash install.sh --verify "$TARGET"', and the npm-registry-unreachable readout (install.sh:2588-2594) prints both 'bash install.sh "$TARGET"' and 'bash install.sh --verify "$TARGET"'. Both sit in the ORDINARY install flow, not the below-floor flow, and step 3 of the procedure IS an ordinary install (bd is at the floor by then). So a curl user on an air-gapped or proxied host who reaches step 3 is handed a local install.sh they do not have -- the same defect class s229 exists to fix. It is NOT on the measured path: the container run's npm ci succeeded (curlpath-e2e-2.log, step 3 reaches the expected rc=3 with beads_ledger FAIL and no npm failure readout).
findings.description: Behaviour is pre-existing and unchanged by this diff, and the procedure's expected path is clean, so this blocks nothing. It raises hevd's value slightly above 'none of them is on the procedure's path', and is worth carrying into hevd's description so v5.0.1 prioritises those two sites over the genuinely off-path ones (--verify on an uninstalled target, --skip-verify).

findings.evidence: NON-BLOCKING. keup is recorded as 'under curl | bash, the EARLY EXITS print curl: (23) Failure writing output to destination'. The measurement shows it on the SUCCESSFUL path too: in curlpath-e2e-2.log, step 4's final check prints the doctor's '13 check(s) -- 12 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped' summary and THEN 'curl: (23) Failure writing output to destination', with the harness recording rc=0 and 'CHECK PASS: the final check exits 0'. Cause is structural, not an early exit: --verify ends in `exec bash "$VERIFY_DOCTOR"` (install.sh:447), so the shell is replaced and curl's remaining write hits a closed pipe.
findings.description: Cosmetic, rc is unaffected. Worth widening keup's description, because the occurrence a teammate actually meets is the LAST line of a successful step 4 -- immediately after 'the doctor then exits 0 with every issue intact' -- which is the worst place for a stray red 'Failure' line.

findings.evidence: NON-BLOCKING. '## [5.0.0] - 2026-10-05' is a forward-dated claim: today is 2026-10-04 (+0700), and the candidate's two commits are dated 10-04. Nothing in the suite checks it -- grep over .claude/scripts/release-claims-check.sh and .claude/scripts/verify-release-manifest.sh finds no CHANGELOG-date assertion, and both specs pass (29 and 83 assertions, rc=0), so their green says nothing about this date.
findings.description: Disclosure (f) owns the decision. Recorded only so it is on the record that `make verify-release` will NOT catch a mismatch: the operator has to confirm the re-cut tag's own date against this line by hand at cut time.

findings.evidence: NON-BLOCKING, precision. The two checkout-detection predicates differ: installer_rerun_cmd requires BOTH `[ -d "$SCRIPT_DIR/.claude/agents" ]` AND `[ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" ]`; Get-InstallerRerunCommand requires only `.claude-plugin\plugin.json`. 9.15 cannot see this because it compares the re-run as the placeholder <RERUN>, and 9.18f only counts Get-InstallerCheckCommand call sites. Both degrade safely in the case that matters: a single downloaded install.sh/install.ps1 (the route docs/QUICKSTART.md:52-53 and :63-64 give) sits in a directory with neither marker, so both fall to the remote form, which is still runnable.
findings.description: No reachable wrong output found. Flagged only because 9.15 exists precisely to stop these two copies drifting, and the one thing it structurally cannot compare is the pair of helpers this change set added. One assertion in v5.0.1 would close it.
